speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. How long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any changes in your appetite or bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those are significant constitutional symptoms. Have you experienced any fever, or have you noticed any lumps in your neck or groin besides the supraclavicular area? I also need to know if there is any blood in your stool or urine. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, LDH, ESR. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CTA, Chest_CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Neck Examination: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed. Abdominal Examination: Slight abdominal distension; Normal bowel sounds; Dullness over left lower quadrant; Splenomegaly without rebound tenderness. Blood Work: Complete Blood Count shows Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, Normal Platelets; Lactate Dehydrogenase is Elevated. Imaging: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen reveals massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy: Cervical Lymph Node shows Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (B-symptom positive with supraclavicular lymphadenopathy and weight loss).
